relevance_note: A WES cohort of 80 children with unexplained liver disease that describes one TNFAIP3 carrier individually: 'One patient with Familial Behçet-Like Autoinflammatory Syndrome caused by a TNFAIP3 mutation received infliximab treatment'.
method_note: Built by hand with a short Python script in scratch; all values come from reading the paper. Only one in-scope person (the single TNFAIP3 case in Group A); 79 other cohort members are out of scope. Label 'unnamed person 1' (rule 6: cohort paper, no label). The variant is said to be in Supplementary Table 1, which is not in this file, so variant_original_string is 'not reported' and all variant-level fields are 'not reported'. Pathogenicity is not reported because the 46 patients with genetic results include both P/LP and VUS carriers and the paper does not say which this person has. Parental testing: WES was done on 'the patients and their parents' as a general method statement, never stated for this person, so parental_testing_statement and inheritance are 'not reported'. Consanguinity 'no' and vital status 'alive' come from statements about the whole cohort ('No consanguineous marriages were found in the cohort.'; 'All patients survived during the follow-up'), a named group that includes this person. The observed feature, liver enzyme elevation, is inferred from the person's assignment to Group A (defined as elevated ALT/AST) and from 'normalization of transaminase levels'. Autoimmune hepatitis is a study exclusion criterion, so it is not used as evidence (checklist left 'not reported'). Ethnicity not recorded: the paper says only that the cohort was recruited at Shandong Provincial Hospital and calls it 'Chinese children' in general statements. Inconsistencies in the paper: the text says genetic results were found in 46 patients but the Figure 2 legend says '45 children'; 42 P/LP plus 7 VUS carriers (49) do not add up to 46. No contradiction about this person.
